In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the innate immune response of epithelial cells of the intestinal tract.
the regulation and function of the innate immune response of intestinal epithelial cells in health and disease.
the regulation of NOD/CARD15 and the consequences of CARD15 mutations for the antibacterial responses of the intestinal epithelial barrier.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CARD15 mutation causes a loss of the NOD2/CAD15 function in the intestinal epithelial cells.
CARD15 is a critical regulator of the epithelial response to bacterial stimuli.
CARD15/NOD2 is not a susceptibility gene for Crohns disease, but rather a gene that is upregulated as a consequence of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CARD15 protein is not constitutively expressed by the normal enterocyte but is inducible in a TLR5 dependent manner by the bacterial flagellin.
the innate immune system is not only important for the defense against pathogens, but also for the maintenance of the homeostasis in the intestine.
NOD2/CAR15 is a sensor molecule for bacterial motifs in the intestinal epitheliam and that CARD15 mutations lead to an impaired antibacterial response in CD patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NOD2/CAD15 is an essential factor of innate immune response in the gut.
NOD2/CAR15 is a key player in the innate immune response of the intestinal epithelia.
NOD2/CAR15 expression is induced by bacterial contact and that this induction is mediated by flagellin‐dependent activation of TLR5.
